title: How to Fix Greyed-Out Middle Eastern Features in InDesign & Illustrator (USA/Canada Guide)
excerpt: Struggling with greyed-out Middle Eastern type options or missing multi-script features in US installations of Adobe InDesign and Illustrator? Learn how to unlock RTL and Arabic/Hebrew text composer settings in under 2 minutes.
targetKeyword: adobe illustrator middle eastern version missing features usa, how to fix indesign middle eastern features greyed out, indesign ME version vs regular version english setup
content:
For graphic designers and layout artists across the United States and Canada, receiving international client assets containing Arabic, Hebrew, or Persian typography often triggers an immediate workflow crisis. When you open an InDesign layout or an Illustrator vector file shipped from a MENA or European partner, the text frequently appears fragmented, reversed, or completely uneditable. More frustratingly, when you attempt to switch text engines, you discover that the Middle Eastern & South Asian paragraph composer options are completely greyed out or missing entirely from your standard English Adobe Creative Cloud installation.

This technical guide explains why US and Canadian software setups restrict multi-script engines by default, how the InDesign ME (Middle Eastern) version differs from standard builds, and the exact steps required to unlock full bidirectional (BiDi) and Cursive OpenType shaping across your entire Adobe suite.

The Core Problem: Why US Creative Cloud Installs Block Multi-Script Features

Adobe packages its desktop software using region-specific language builds to optimize memory allocation and streamline regional dictionary installations. Standard North American Creative Cloud deployments install the Latin and East Asian (LE) text engine by default. While this engine handles English, French, Spanish, and basic European diacritics flawlessly, it lacks the underlying OpenType shaping tables required for:

  1. Complex Cursive Positioning (GPOS/GSUB): Dynamic ligatures that alter character shapes depending on whether a letter appears at the initial, medial, final, or isolated position within an Arabic word.
  2. Bidirectional (BiDi) Text Flow: The Unicode bidirectional algorithm required to intermix Right-to-Left (RTL) Arabic/Hebrew script with Left-to-Right (LTR) English numbers and punctuation without breaking sentence order.
  3. World-Ready Composers: Advanced justification and line-breaking algorithms designed specifically for multi-script editorial layouts.

InDesign ME Version vs. Regular English Setup: What Actually Changes?

Many designers assume they need to download a completely separate, foreign-language version of Adobe InDesign or Illustrator. Historically, Adobe maintained distinct "Middle Eastern versions" (ME versions) of its software. However, modern Creative Cloud architecture (v23.0 through 2026) uses a Unified Application Core.

Instead of maintaining two separate apps, your existing US English installation already contains all global language engines. They are simply locked behind your Creative Cloud installation preferences and panel flyout menus. Unlocking them transforms your standard English workspace into a fully bilingual, multi-script environment.

Step-by-Step Resolution: Unlocking Middle Eastern Features in InDesign & Illustrator

Follow these precise steps to activate multi-script text engines across your US or Canadian Creative Cloud setup:

Step 1: Modify Creative Cloud Default Install Language

  1. Save your active projects and close all Adobe applications (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop).
  2. Open the Adobe Creative Cloud Desktop App on your workstation.
  3. Click your profile avatar in the top-right corner and select Preferences.
  4. Navigate to the Apps tab on the left sidebar.
  5. Locate the Default Install Language dropdown menu. Instead of standard English, select English (Supports Arabic) or English (Supports Hebrew).
  6. Allow Creative Cloud to update your application language dictionaries. (Note: This does not change your software user interface language; it only injects the missing multi-script dictionaries and composer modules).

Step 2: Enable World-Ready Composers Inside InDesign

Once your application environment is re-initialized, you must activate the correct paragraph composer for your imported international files:

  1. Launch Adobe InDesign and open your document.
  2. Open the Paragraph panel by navigating to Window > Type & Tables > Paragraph.
  3. Click the panel flyout menu in the upper-right corner (four horizontal lines).
  4. Under the Paragraph Composer sub-menu, select Adobe World-Ready Paragraph Composer (or Middle Eastern & South Asian Single-line Composer).
  5. Open the Character panel and ensure your language dropdown is explicitly set to an Arabic or Hebrew variant to enable correct hyphenation and spelling rules.
Composer Setting Supported Scripts Ideal Use Case in North American Workflows
Adobe Paragraph Composer Latin, Cyrillic, Greek (LTR only) Standard US/Canadian English and European print layouts.
Adobe World-Ready Composer Multi-script (Arabic, Hebrew, Indic, Latin) Bilingual corporate reports, localized product packaging, and international design handoffs.

Handling Rasterized Proofs and Web Conversion Workflows

If you are collaborating with remote international teams and receive flattened PDF proofs, scanned client briefs, or rasterized images instead of live InDesign files, native paragraph composers will not help you extract editable text. Attempting to copy strings directly from flattened bitmaps results in broken Unicode characters.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Why are Middle Eastern paragraph options greyed out in my US version of InDesign?

Middle Eastern text engines are greyed out because your Creative Cloud app was installed using a standard Latin-only language pack. Changing your Creative Cloud default install language to include Arabic or Hebrew support unlocks these greyed-out options instantly.

Do I need to reinstall Adobe InDesign entirely to get ME features?

No full reinstallation is required. Updating your Creative Cloud language preferences injects the necessary dictionary and composer modules into your existing application directories upon relaunch.

How do I handle documents that mix English (LTR) and Arabic (RTL) text blocks?

By enabling the **Adobe World-Ready Paragraph Composer** and setting your paragraph direction controls correctly, InDesign automatically handles bidirectional text flow, ensuring numbers, punctuation marks, and embedded English words maintain correct reading order.

Can I open Arabic InDesign files created in Dubai or Riyadh on a standard US workstation?

Yes, provided you have enabled Middle Eastern language support in your Creative Cloud preferences. Once unlocked, your US installation will correctly interpret all OpenType ligature tables and story threads from international files.
